rows.source_population: adults living with glaucoma interviewed on everyday disease management in Nigeria (qualitative study; quote from participant G03)
rows.family_population: 66-year-old adult with dark brown skin whose routine optometry exam measured bilateral eye pressure of 28 mmHg
rows.note: Same older-adult darker-skin glaucoma / ocular-hypertension population; verbatim patient phrase 'your eye pressure' adapted to first-person 'my eye pressure'.

rows.source_population: adults diagnosed with oral leukoplakia and other oral potentially malignant disorders at an oral medicine clinic in Hyderabad, India (qualitative interview study; quote from 32-year-old male oral leukoplakia patient)
rows.family_population: adult 25-year daily cigarette smoker with a 6-week rough adherent white patch on the left lateral tongue
rows.note: Same adult oral leukoplakia / oral potentially malignant mucosal disorder population; verbatim patient phrase 'this white patch' adapted to 'a white patch'.

rows.expression: and I think I bit my tongue
rows.source_population: 35 adult oral cancer patients interviewed on pre-presentation symptom interpretation and delayed health-seeking across six regional centers in Malaysia (quote from 35-year-old male patient)
rows.family_population: adult 25-year daily cigarette smoker with a 6-week rough adherent white patch on the left lateral tongue
rows.note: Same adult oral tongue lesion population; verbatim patient causal misattribution 'I felt like I accidentally bit my tongue' adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think I bit my tongue'.

rows.source_population: 20 working adults with ADHD interviewed by telephone in Sweden regarding workplace functioning and work-related stress
rows.family_population: working adult with childhood-onset sustained attention difficulties refractory to 8 weeks of daily primary-care focus medication
rows.note: Same working-adult ADHD population; authors' thematic summary phrase 'not keeping up with tasks' adapted into positive difficulty phrasing 'keeping up with work tasks'.

rows.source_population: 20 working adults with ADHD interviewed by telephone in Sweden regarding workplace functioning and work-related stress
rows.family_population: working adult with childhood-onset sustained attention difficulties refractory to 8 weeks of daily primary-care focus medication
rows.note: Same working-adult ADHD population; authors' thematic summary phrase 'difficulties staying focused' adapted to 'trouble staying focused'.

rows.source_population: adult outpatients with ADHD inattentive presentation interviewed after group CBT in Stockholm, Sweden
rows.family_population: working adult with childhood-onset sustained attention difficulties refractory to 8 weeks of daily primary-care focus medication
rows.note: Same adult inattentive-ADHD outpatient population; authors' report that participants 'often felt they were lazy' adapted into first-person causal belief clause 'and I think I'm lazy'.

rows.expression: constant intense grief that affects my daily life
rows.source_population: 18 bereaved widowers recruited from five outpatient clinics in Taiwan and interviewed on grief experiences and prolonged grief disorder (quote C12)
rows.family_population: 70-year-old widower experiencing persistent functionally impairing grief 16 months after his wife's death
rows.note: Same bereaved widower outpatient population discussing prolonged grief disorder; verbatim widower quote 'Being constantly trapped in grief can affect normal daily life.' adapted into non-idiomatic first-person 'constant intense grief that affects my daily life'.

rows.expression: severe pelvic pain keeping me in bed
rows.source_population: 12 employed reproductive-age women predominantly diagnosed with endometriosis interviewed in Australia regarding symptom impact on daily life and work (Participant 7)
rows.family_population: 29-year-old woman with severe monthly pelvic pain confining her to bed despite 12 months of menstrual ibuprofen use
rows.note: Same reproductive-age endometriosis population; verbatim patient expressions 'in bed for the first two days' and 'from the pelvic pain' combined into 'severe pelvic pain keeping me in bed'.

rows.expression: and I think I just have really bad periods
rows.source_population: reproductive-age U.S. Black women diagnosed with endometriosis interviewed on symptom experience and quality of life (quote from Casey, aged 26-35 years)
rows.family_population: 29-year-old woman with severe monthly pelvic pain confining her to bed despite 12 months of menstrual ibuprofen use
rows.note: Same reproductive-age (26-35 years) endometriosis population; verbatim pre-diagnosis normalization quote 'I just thought I had really bad periods.' adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think I just have really bad periods'.

rows.source_population: 340 adult outpatients aged 30-75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus at primary and secondary care centers in Karachi, Pakistan (cross-sectional symptom comparison by dyslipidemia status)
rows.family_population: overweight 48-year-old adult with 3 weeks of new-onset frequent urination and excessive thirst
rows.note: Same adult outpatient type 2 diabetes / hyperglycemia demographic (age 48 within 30-75 years, higher-weight metabolic profile); authors report 'frequent urination' verbatim as a prevalent patient symptom.

rows.source_population: 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presenting to the emergency room with acute hyperglycemia, shortness of breath, frequent urination, and excessive thirst during COVID-19 infection (case report)
rows.family_population: overweight 48-year-old adult with 3 weeks of new-onset frequent urination and excessive thirst
rows.note: Source reports a 58-year-old woman with established type 2 diabetes describing acute 1-day emergency hyperglycemic symptoms ('excessive thirst' verbatim), adapted here to a 48-year-old adult with 3 weeks of subacute outpatient polyuria and polydipsia.

rows.source_population: 19 adults who had lived with palmar hyperhidrosis for >10 years with work, study, and daily-life functional limitations (qualitative interview study)
rows.family_population: 26-year-old adult office worker with daily bilateral palmar sweating soaking work papers for 6 weeks
rows.note: Same adult palmar hyperhidrosis population experiencing occupational and daily-life impairment; authors' qualitative summary phrase 'excessive hand sweating' is adapted to 'daily sweating on both palms'.

rows.source_population: 60-year-old man presenting as an outpatient with itchy, scaly upper-back lesions clinically consistent with tinea corporis (dermatology case report)
rows.family_population: adult gym-mat user with an expanding itchy scaly ring-shaped chest patch refractory to hydrocortisone cream
rows.note: Same adult outpatient truncal dermatophytosis (tinea corporis) presentation; 'itchy' used verbatim.

rows.source_population: 34-year-old woman referred by her general practitioner to ENT for intermittent left-ear muffled hearing, later diagnosed with vertebral artery dissection / Bow Hunter's syndrome (case report)
rows.family_population: 71-year-old adult with unilateral left-ear plugging and muffled hearing 5 days after cotton-swab use
rows.note: Source describes a younger (34-year-old) primary-care patient referred to ENT for unilateral left-ear 'muffled hearing' (subsequently found to have vascular pathology), adapted here to a 71-year-old adult with unilateral left-ear muffled hearing after cotton-swab earwax impaction.

rows.source_population: 37-year-old man presenting 2 weeks after an inversion ankle sprain with persistent posterolateral ankle pain and walking instability (case report)
rows.family_population: adult walking slowly with persistent outer right ankle pain and mild swelling 10 days after an inward right ankle roll
rows.note: Same adult subacute post-inversion-sprain outpatient presentation (10 days vs 2 weeks post-injury); 'ankle pain' used verbatim.

rows.source_population: 45-year-old woman presenting with a popliteal venous aneurysm, deep muscle branch venous reflux, and leg heaviness 26 years after lower-extremity rhabdomyosarcoma resection (vascular surgery case report)
rows.family_population: adult standing retail worker with 6 months of bilateral lower-leg varicose veins and evening leg heaviness
rows.note: Both are adults presenting with lower-extremity venous reflux and 'leg heaviness' (used verbatim), adapted from a post-oncologic popliteal venous aneurysm/perforator reflux case to primary bilateral lower-leg superficial varicose veins in a retail worker.

rows.expression: a sudden tearing misery in my back
rows.source_population: US and UK dialect English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'misery', Noun sense 2; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 66-year-old US or UK dialect English speaker on cholesterol therapy developing acute tearing interscapular back pain
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('A bodily ache or pain' in US and UK dialects, matching dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general dialect lexical meaning rather than a clinical aortic-dissection patient cohort; embedded into 'a sudden tearing misery in my back'.

rows.source_population: UK adults (explicitly noting one-third of people aged >65 years) presenting to physicians with dizziness, imbalance, and 'funny turns' (Royal College of Physicians conference review)
rows.family_population: 67-year-old British or Australian English speaker with persistent twice-weekly brief spinning vertigo episodes ('funny turns') and mild walking unsteadiness
rows.note: Same older-adult (>65 years) UK clinical population presenting with dizziness, imbalance, and quoted patient complaint 'funny turns' (used verbatim).

rows.source_population: English speakers using colloquial/dialect adjective 'swimmy' (Wiktionary lexical entry 'swimmy', Adjective sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 71-year-old older adult experiencing postural lightheadedness 1 week after an antihypertensive dose increase
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('Dizzy; swirling or moving as if seen in a daze', matching dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than an older-adult orthostatic-hypotension cohort; combined into unhyphenated 'swimmy headed'.

rows.source_population: English speakers using colloquial/dialect adjective 'swimmy' (Wiktionary lexical entry 'swimmy', Adjective sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 71-year-old older adult experiencing postural lightheadedness 1 week after an antihypertensive dose increase
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('Dizzy; swirling or moving as if seen in a daze', matching dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than an older-adult orthostatic-hypotension cohort; embedded into 'my head feels swimmy'.

rows.source_population: 426 patients aged 7-84 years (mean 38.4 years) referred for tilt-table testing of suspected neurally mediated syncope at a tertiary heart center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
rows.family_population: US colloquial English parent describing a 14-year-old daughter with recurrent brief orthostatic dizzy spells during warm school assemblies
rows.note: Cohort spans ages 7-84 years (including adolescents) with suspected neurally mediated syncope/presyncope and reports 'dizzy spells' verbatim, but comes from an English-language cardiology report in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia rather than a US parent/adolescent setting (US colloquial label comes from Wiktionary in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json).
